meta.notes: Hero, nav chrome and the 'Version 3.1 The Long Goodbye' splash sub-page were directly viewed and their CSS/computed styles inspected live (font-family, @font-face, and colour census pulled from the site's actual stylesheets — [observed: CSS] tier). Below the hero, the homepage runs a scroll-linked WebGL/canvas background (character carousel, videos, news, footer) that this sandboxed browser could not paint — those sections render blank screenshots even though the DOM/assets load correctly. Component-level shape/elevation/texture claims for anything below the hero are therefore [inferred] from HoYoverse-genre norms, not pixel-observed, and are flagged as such throughout. statusPositive and statusCaution have no native brand equivalent on the pages that did render and are derived to match the brand's high-saturation neon-on-black mood — flagged per rule 15.

essence.positioning: A hyper-saturated urban-noir action game that treats its own patch notes like TV episodes and its UI chrome like a corporate operations terminal.

voice.source: live copy read from https://zenless.hoyoverse.com/en-us/main and the in-app 'Version 3.1 The Long Goodbye' splash sub-page via browser
voice.summary: Speaks like an in-world ops broadcast, not a marketing page — exact timestamps, named 'episodes' for each update, and rarity-tier lexicon (S-Rank, W-Engine) doing double duty as both game terms and sales pitch.

pillars.name: Narrative episode naming for routine updates
pillars.evidence: The Zenless Zone Zero Version 3.2 "Their Secret Histories" Special Program will begin on August 28 at 19:30 (UTC+8)!

pillars.name: Rarity-tier lexicon as the sales pitch itself

voice.person: second-person via UI address, but 'you' is rarely spelled out — the brand prefers naming the place/role over naming the reader (e.g. addressing arrival at a location rather than saying 'welcome, player') [observed] the literal in-lore player title was not present in the captured copy, so it is not asserted here
voice.cadence: measured and logistical even at its most excited — exact UTC+8 timestamps and version numbers sit right next to bold display type; at most one exclamation mark per announcement, never stacked; ALL-CAPS reserved for platform/rating chrome ("AVAILABLE ON") not for voice
voice.commerceVoice: Purchase/login incentives are framed as narrative rarity ("a Limited S-Rank Agent") rather than a price cut, paired with an exact, almost bureaucratic time-window rather than vague urgency language.

contrastRules: Primary CTA: black text (#000) on #D8FA00 neon — extremely high contrast, ~15.6:1, comfortably clears AA for any text size.
Nav/header: white wordmark on #000000 — ~21:1, maximum contrast, matches the brand's 'contrast is king' chrome instinct.
Body canvas is a light #EFEFEF grey, not pure white — dark UI chrome (#000) sits on it at ~19:1; this is the one light-mode surface observed outside the dark hero/splash frames.

No text-on-key-art contrast pairing was directly observable (scroll-blocked sections) — when placing type over character art, default to the brand's own instinct: solid black or near-black scrim block behind type rather than a soft gradient scrim, matching the flat black platform-badge bar under the hero.

assetPrompts.heroBanner: Cel-shaded 3D-render anime key art, two stylish urban operatives leaning on a parked car in a rain-washed industrial alley at dusk, neon signage reflections, cool blue-grey environment palette contrasted against one small saturated neon-yellow-green accent light; clean line work, soft ambient occlusion, no painterly grain; 16:9 landscape composition with open negative space in the lower-left third for logo lockup and CTA.
assetPrompts.skuArt: Single cel-shaded anime character, ¾ bust framing, dynamic asymmetric pose, flat dark neutral studio backdrop with one rim-light in the brand's neon yellow-green (#D8FA00), portrait 2:3 crop, clean vector-sharp edges, no background clutter.
assetPrompts.background: Seamless dark near-black (#0A0A0A) tile with a faint diagonal comic-panel cut line in low-contrast dark grey — no dot/halftone texture, no visible grain; reads as a clean industrial backdrop at any tile size.

codashop.architectureNote: 5-tier cascade: (1) type primitives + ref seeds → (2) palette ramps (--x-palette-{role}-500 = --x-ref-{role}) → (3) sys intensity / dimensions / effects / states → (4) semantic defaults (--x-bg-*, --x-text-*, --x-border-*) → (5) .text-style-* classes. Figma token exports drop the --x- prefix; repo names always include it. emitter.ts injects only Tier 1 ref seeds + optional Tier 2 ramps + font + --x-bg-page. Tiers 3-4 auto-resolve downstream and are store-overridable. THREE override layers: SYSTEM CONSTANT (layoutSystem + the 27 textStyle compositions + scales — never change) ⊃ BRAND-LOCKED (ref seeds, font, size values, brandCharacter) ⊃ STORE-FLEXIBLE (semantic colour mapping, component variants).

layoutSystem.containerRule: device screen sets container-type:inline-size; overlay must NOT (traps position:fixed)

spanVariants.content: full width on XS/S; centred cols 3–10 of 12, max-width 960px, on M/L
spanVariants.carousel: full-bleed on XS/S (negative margin cancels grid margin); content on M/L

layoutSystem.tokenTierDiscipline: components consume ONLY semantic (--x-bg-*, --x-text-*, --x-border-*) + spacing/size (--x-pad-*, --x-gap-*, --x-radius-*, --x-size-*); NEVER --x-sys-*, --x-palette-*, or --x-ref-* directly
layoutSystem.mobileDesktopRule: values switch at breakpoints via -desktop- token twins: --x-sys-space-desktop-*, --x-sys-radius-desktop-*, --x-sys-size-control-desktop-*, --x-text-size-desktop-*

palette.anchorRule: --x-palette-{role}-500 resolves to --x-ref-{role} — the 500 step IS the seed
